plain_text:
New research funded by the
National Institutes of Health has
found that kidneys of those who
have died with HIV can safely be
transplanted into people living with
both HIV and end-stage kidney
disease. NIH’s National Institute
of Allergy and Infectious Diseases
and the National Cancer Institute
both funded the study. It builds on
important 2019 research that found
that people living with HIV who
received kidney transplants from
deceased donors with HIV had high
overall survival after five years.

It builds on important 2019 research that found that people living with HIV who received kidney transplants from deceased donors with HIV had high overall survival after five years.
